questions.stem: In which conditions of visibility do the Rules in Section I (Rules 4 to 10) apply?
options: Only in good visibility
Only in restricted visibility
Only at night
In any condition of visibility
questions.explanation: Rule 4 says the Rules in Section I apply in any condition of visibility, whether it is clear daylight, darkness or fog.

questions.stem: Which of these Rules belongs to Section I and so applies whatever the visibility?
options: Rule 5, keeping a proper lookout
Rule 13, overtaking
Rule 14, head-on situations
Rule 15, crossing situations
questions.explanation: Rules 4 to 10 form Section I, and Rule 5 (lookout) is one of them. Rules 13, 14 and 15 are in Section II, which applies to vessels in sight of one another.

questions.stem: When do the Rules in Section II (Rules 11 to 18) apply?
options: In any condition of visibility
Only when vessels are in sight of one another
Only when a vessel has radar
Only in narrow channels
questions.explanation: Section II covers the conduct of vessels in sight of one another. In sight means one can be seen visually from the other. Section I applies in any visibility, and radar or channel width does not decide Section II.

questions.stem: In heavy fog you are tracking another vessel on radar only, and cannot see her. Which statement is correct?
options: Section II governs, because radar counts as being in sight
Only Section III applies, and Rules 5 to 10 no longer apply
Section III's Rule 19 governs the situation, and Section I (including lookout, safe speed and risk of collision) still applies
No Rules apply until you see the other vessel
questions.explanation: Vessels are in sight only when seen visually, so Section II does not apply. Rule 19 deals with restricted visibility, and Section I applies in any condition of visibility, so it applies alongside Rule 19.

questions.stem: A trainee says, "Rule 6 on safe speed is a bad-weather rule, so on a clear day I can ignore it." Which reply is best?
options: Incorrect, because Rule 6 is in Section I and applies in any condition of visibility
Correct, because Rule 6 applies only in restricted visibility
Correct, because safe speed matters only at night
Incorrect, but only when other vessels are within one mile
questions.explanation: Rule 6 is in Section I, which Rule 4 says applies in any condition of visibility. Visibility is one of the factors in judging safe speed, but it does not decide whether the Rule applies. There is no distance trigger in Rule 6 either.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly describes Section III of the Steering and Sailing Rules?
options: It is Rule 19, and applies to vessels not in sight of one another when navigating in or near an area of restricted visibility
It is Rules 11 to 18, and applies only at night
It is Rule 19, and applies to every vessel whenever it is foggy anywhere on the coast, even vessels in sight of each other
It is Rules 4 to 10, and applies only in clear weather
questions.explanation: Section III is Rule 19, conduct of vessels in restricted visibility. It applies to vessels not in sight of one another when navigating in or near an area of restricted visibility. Vessels that can see each other use Section II (Rules 11 to 18), and Section I (Rules 4 to 10) applies in any condition of visibility, not only in clear weather.
